recommendations.text: Investigate the telemetry pipeline to identify the root cause of per-car laps appearing out of driving order after roughly eighteen hours of running, and fix the cause rather than merely reordering the displayed laps.

Establish from the repository how telemetry timing and sequence values are decoded, compared, and used to update race state and lap ordering. Investigate long-duration boundary behavior, including overflow, rollover, precision loss, and delayed or out-of-order telemetry, without assuming which is responsible.

Add a deterministic regression test that reproduces the identified long-session failure through the relevant telemetry-to-race-state path. Use simulated timestamps or telemetry sequences where feasible rather than requiring an eighteen-hour real-time run.

The regression test must fail against the unfixed implementation and pass with the fix, asserting that the affected car's laps retain their actual driving order across the identified failure boundary.
Keep the change focused on the identified telemetry-pipeline defect and preserve existing behavior for ordinary-duration sessions.

Verify the regression test's before-and-after results and run the repository's applicable test suite. The supplied snapshot lists npm test as the test command; confirm the current test setup in the repository and report any failures or verification limitations.

spec.rawIntent: In long sessions the race state gets corrupted: after roughly eighteen hours of running, laps of a car appear out of driving order. Find the cause in the telemetry pipeline and fix it, with a test that fails before the fix.
